entries.title: Polynomial-corrected binary/unary tree
entries.statement: For a fixed real beta, let N=ceil(8(1+abs(beta))), B_n=floor(n/2+beta*log_2(1+n/N)), and let T_beta be the rooted tree with 2^(B_(n+1)-B_n) children at each vertex at depth n. The root has depth zero; all edges are undirected. This defines the tree family used for the critical-survival boundary examples.

entries.title: Reciprocal survival bound for binary/unary trees
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT; INDEPENDENT MATHEMATICAL REVIEW PENDING. In an independent Bernoulli-p bond model on a spherically symmetric rooted tree with a_i in {1,2} children at depth i, let q_n be root connection probability to level n, m_0=1, m_j=p^j*product_(i<j)a_i, and S_n=sum_(i<n:a_i=2)1/m_i. For 0<p<=1 and finite n, 1/m_n+S_n/4 <= 1/q_n <= 1/m_n+S_n/[4(1-p/2)]. The proof telescopes the exact one- or two-child survival recursion using disjoint descendant edge sets. This is a special-case calculation, not a recursion for graphs with overlapping branches.

entries.title: Sharp polynomial boundary for critical tree survival
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT; INDEPENDENT MATHEMATICAL REVIEW PENDING. For a fixed real beta, let N=ceil(8(1+abs(beta))), B_n=floor(n/2+beta*log_2(1+n/N)), and let T_beta be the rooted tree with 2^(B_(n+1)-B_n) children at each vertex at depth n. T_beta has maximum degree at most 3 and p_c=1/sqrt(2). At criticality the root survival probability is positive exactly when beta>1. For beta<1, root connection probability to depth n is comparable to n^(beta-1); for beta=1 it is comparable to 1/log(n), for large n with beta-dependent constants. For beta>1, theta_o(p_c)>=(2-1/sqrt(2))/(1+N/(beta-1)); in particular theta_(T_2)(p_c)>=(2-1/sqrt(2))/25. When beta<=1 there is almost surely no infinite cluster anywhere. Each T_beta has a unique leaf, its root, and is not quasi-transitive. Thus this example does not refute critical extinction on quasi-transitive graphs.
assumptions: tree family defined explicitly in this statement

entries.title: Critical extinction fails to pass to general local limits
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT; INDEPENDENT MATHEMATICAL REVIEW PENDING. Let T be the rooted tree with B_n=floor(n/2+2*log_2(1+n/24)) and 2^(B_(n+1)-B_n) children at depth n. Let T^(K) use the same offspring counts for i<K and then alternate 1,2 children forever. All these connected trees have maximum degree 3 and p_c=1/sqrt(2). Each T^(K) has no infinite cluster at criticality, but T has positive critical root survival. The rooted balls of T^(K) converge to those of T. Equal critical parameters therefore do not allow critical extinction to pass to local limits of arbitrary bounded-degree rooted graphs. None of these examples is quasi-transitive.

entries.title: Equal-threshold quasi-isometry obstruction to critical extinction
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT; INDEPENDENT MATHEMATICAL REVIEW PENDING. For a fixed real beta, let N=ceil(8(1+abs(beta))), B_n=floor(n/2+beta*log_2(1+n/N)), and let T_beta be the rooted tree with 2^(B_(n+1)-B_n) children at each vertex at depth n. Contract unary corridors to the rooted binary branching skeleton. Each corridor and the initial stem have length at most 4; the resulting surjection pi obeys d_binary(pi(u),pi(v))<=d_T(u,v)<=4*d_binary(pi(u),pi(v))+8. Hence every T_beta is quasi-isometric to the rooted binary tree. T_0 and T_2 have equal critical probability 1/sqrt(2), yet only T_0 has critical extinction. Critical extinction is not a quasi-isometry invariant for arbitrary bounded-degree graphs, even with equal critical parameters. No claim is made about invariance within quasi-transitive graphs.
assumptions: tree family defined explicitly in this statement

entries.title: Unproved symmetry-to-extinction exploration bridge
entries.statement: UNPROVED ROUTE DIAGNOSIS; current openness UNKNOWN. The target is absence of all infinite critical Bernoulli bond clusters on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with p_c<1. A possible proof route would derive a sufficient finite-scale extinction or exploration-comparison criterion in subexponential growth. The missing step is preserving conditional exposure control when graph exploration branches overlap. A binary/unary tree survival recursion requires disjoint descendant randomness, and exponential level-growth rates alone cannot exclude polynomial corrections causing critical survival. No such comparison is proved in this packet; recent claims of the full target have not been independently audited here.
assumptions: infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph

relations.rationale: The threshold is stated for the explicitly defined T_beta family.
The author proof applies the two-sided reciprocal bound at p=1/sqrt(2).
The limit T_2 survives by the beta>1 criterion; periodic tails die by the same reciprocal bound.
At criticality periodic tail means are bounded and the branching reciprocal sum diverges.
The two quasi-isometric examples are T_0 and T_2, with the contrasting critical survival established in the author tree proof.
The bounded-degree tree example demonstrates why exponential growth rates alone are insufficient outside quasi-transitivity.
